chapter: Entertainers, Creole Serenaders and La Vida
title: Working conditions and pay at La Vida taxi dance hall
summary: The job ran nonstop; pay was low during the Depression with ten cents a dance. The hostesses worked on percentage.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: That was the whole job, huh? Oh man, it started at eight o'clock or four o'clock in the morning. Constantly playing. Never stopped, you know. I mean the trumpet would pick up one chorus, then the sax would pick up the next chorus. Did you make much money there?
No, they wasn't paying too much.
They didn't do any depression, you see.
That was about the only job you could get, man.

They had other little jobs opening, you know, but that was about one of the best regular jobs, you see. Regular, that's the man thing. They wasn't paying but two fifteen at night, yeah. Did you make much tips? Not there. Ten cents a dance, you know.
But what happened with the women there? They were getting their ten cents, huh?
Well, they worked on percentage. They worked on percentage, just calling how many drinks and the tickets there.
You think there was a lot of prostitution there too?
Well, I don't know about that part of it, playing and I can't tell you what was going on.
